— **Sahil Kapur**, NBC News Senior National Political Reporter

> "I don't think that Donald Trump is going to allow a ceasefire to remain for very long if there's going to be firing on ships... the United States is taking full advantage... to make sure we identify targets... and end this thing once and for all the hard way."
— **Sen. Kevin Cramer**, (R-N.D.)

briefings.title: One Brain, Any Robot: Skild AI's Skild Brain Explained | NVIDIA AI Podcast Ep. 295
briefings.tldr: Skild AI is developing "Skild Brain," a foundational, general-purpose AI model designed to power any robot form factor—from humanoid to industrial arms—using a shared "Omni-bodied" intelligence that scales through a multi-layered data flywheel.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Skild AI is developing "Skild Brain," a foundational, general-purpose AI model designed to power any robot form factor—from humanoid to industrial arms—using a shared "Omni-bodied" intelligence that scales through a multi-layered data flywheel.

## The Shift to Horizontal Robotics
*   **Omni-bodied Intelligence:** Skild is moving away from "vertical" robotics (where software is custom-built for one specific task, like welding) toward a horizontal platform.
    *   **General-purpose Brain:** Similar to how Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a base for various text applications, Skild Brain serves as a universal controller that can be fine-tuned for specific industrial or consumer needs.
*   **Addressing the "Corner Case" Problem:** Traditional robotics often hits a performance wall at 90% because of unpredictable real-world variables. 
    *   By using a shared brain, a "corner case" in one industry (e.g., a misplaced box in a warehouse) becomes a "central case" the AI has already learned to handle in another environment.
*   **Learning vs. Programming:** The company is shifting the engineering focus from "how a robot should move" to "how a robot can learn from data," allowing for deployment in unmeasured, unstructured environments like homes and hospitals.

## The Three-Layer Data Strategy
Because there is no "internet of robot data," Skild utilizes a tiered approach to train its models:
*   **Video Pre-training (Diversity):** Leveraging billions of real-world videos to teach the model general physics and task concepts. While scalable, this data lacks "richness" (specific force and motor command data).
*   **Simulation (Scale):** Using simulators to collect trillions of data points.
    *   **Sim-to-Real Gap:** Simulation provides the "practice" needed to make behaviors robust, though it requires algorithmic bridging to work in the physical world.
*   **Real-world Post-training (Precision):** Collecting high-quality teleoperation data from real robots. This is the most expensive data to gather but is essential for "post-training" the model to perform specific, high-precision tasks in factories or warehouses.

## The Data Flywheel & Deployment Roadmap
*   **Continuous Improvement:** Every robot deployed contributes data back to the central brain. As the fleet grows, the amount of data required to teach the brain a new task decreases.
*   **Deployment Phases:**
    *   **Phase 1 (Current):** Structured/Semi-structured industrial environments (factories and warehouses) where tasks are repeatable but require AI for adaptability.
    *   **Phase 2 (Near-term):** Unstructured service environments, including hospitals, hotels, and grocery stores.
    *   **Phase 3 (Long-term):** Unstructured consumer environments (home robots).
*   **Deployment as a Technical Hurdle:** Unlike software, physical AI deployment is a distinct technical challenge. Skild focuses on "specializing" the general model for new partners in a matter of days rather than months.

## NVIDIA Partnership and Infrastructure
*   **Simulation and Solvers:** Skild uses NVIDIA Isaac Sim and is co-developing advanced physics solvers (Newton) to improve simulation accuracy.
*   **Generative AI for Augmentation:** The company leverages NVIDIA Cosmos and other video models for data augmentation, creating multiple variations of a single data point to increase model robustness.
*   **Edge Computing:** Because robots require near-instantaneous reaction times to prevent falling or accidents, Skild partners with NVIDIA to utilize high-performance on-device edge compute rather than relying on cloud processing.

## Notable Quotes

> "Robotics is a data problem. Unlike language or vision, there is not much data in robotics. There is no internet of robot data. So if that's the scenario, we cannot pick and choose which data we use." — **Deepak Pathak, CEO**

> "We are building this horizontal general-purpose brain... our thesis is that a corner case of one vertical becomes the central case of the other vertical. Now the data is from everywhere, and it will be able to handle these corner cases through the data flywheel." — **Abhinav Gupta, President**

> "In the longer timeline, we will be able to automate every single action that humans can take in the physical world. We are following the approach which is very similar to how things actually happened in nature." — **Deepak Pathak, CEO**

> "The progress of compute and the hardware costs coming down has just made this all so surprising that even experts like us who have been working in this for 20 years are scared to say anything [about timelines] online." — **Abhinav Gupta, President**

briefings.title: OpenAI Co-Founder on the AI Race, the Sam Altman Firing, and What Comes Next
briefings.tldr: OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman details the organization’s evolution from a resource-constrained non-profit to a global AI leader, highlighting the necessity of massive compute scaling, the internal resilience required to survive the 2023 board crisis, and a future where agentic AI serves as a personalized partner for billions.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman details the organization’s evolution from a resource-constrained non-profit to a global AI leader, highlighting the necessity of massive compute scaling, the internal resilience required to survive the 2023 board crisis, and a future where agentic AI serves as a personalized partner for billions.

## The Genesis and Evolution of OpenAI
* **Founding Mission (2015):** Brockman left Stripe to co-found OpenAI with Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever, and John Schulman. The goal was to ensure human-level AI benefited all of humanity, despite the field being dominated at the time by "10,000-pound gorilla" Google DeepMind.
* **The For-Profit Pivot (2017):**
    * **Compute Realization:** In 2017, the team calculated the compute power necessary for AGI and realized it was far beyond non-profit fundraising capabilities.
    * **Hardware Catalyst:** A meeting with Cerebras, which was building advanced AI hardware, convinced leadership that exclusive access to massive data centers was the only path to success, necessitating a for-profit structure.
* **Early Technical Roadmap:** The original "technical plan" involved three pillars: solving reinforcement learning, solving unsupervised learning, and gradually learning "more complicated things."

## Breakthroughs in Scaling and Reasoning
* **The Dota 2 Milestone:** Brockman identifies the Dota results as a turning point. It proved that "massive compute with simple algorithms" (PPO) could exceed human performance in messy, unprogrammed environments.
    * **The "Insect Brain" Insight:** The neural net used for Dota had synapses comparable to an insect brain; scaling this to human-brain proportions became the evocative goal for the GPT series.
* **Prediction as Intelligence:** Brockman argues that "predicting the next word" is not a pedestrian task. If a model can perfectly predict the next word out of Einstein’s mouth, it possesses Einstein-level intelligence.
* **The 2017 "Sentiment Neuron":** A key breakthrough occurred when a model trained purely on next-character prediction spontaneously learned "sentiment" (semantics), proving that machines could learn meaning without explicit supervision.
* **AI-Driven Engineering:** 
    * **Software Production:** Brockman notes that the fraction of OpenAI code *not* written by AI is "vanishing." AI currently writes code better than humans given the right context.
    * **Scientific Discovery:** Models are now solving open math and physics problems, including resolving a quantum physics problem with an elegant formula that contradicted community expectations.

## Leadership and the 2023 Board Crisis
* **The Firing Event:** Brockman was informed of Sam Altman’s removal via a board video call (minus Altman). He was told he was removed from the board but asked to stay; he quit immediately after speaking with his wife.
* **Team Loyalty:** 
    * **The "Life Raft":** Initially, Brockman and Altman planned a small new venture, but the entire company rebelled.
    * **Unprecedented Retention:** Despite "feeding frenzy" poaching attempts from competitors, OpenAI did not lose a single employee during the weekend of the ouster.
* **Reconciliation with Ilya Sutskever:** Brockman describes the pain of the conflict with Sutskever—who had been the officiant at his wedding—but notes they reached "closure" through intense post-crisis communication.

## The Future: Agentic AGI and Global Compute
* **From Tools to Agents:** The next phase shifts from humans doing work *with* computers to computers doing work *for* humans. 
    * **Universal Access:** Brockman envisions 8 billion people having a "personal AGI" that knows their context, manages their goals, and takes proactive actions (e.g., buying concert tickets or solving health issues).
* **Industrial-Scale Data Centers:** Brockman expects to see data centers dedicated entirely to single problems, such as "solving cancer."
    * **Grand Challenges:** He suggests data centers in space are a "grand challenge" due to the fragility of current hardware, but "all options" are on the table to meet the exponential demand for compute.
* **Iterative Deployment:** OpenAI rejects the "ivory tower" approach of building in secret. Brockman argues that deploying intermediate models (like GPT-3 and GPT-4) allows society to build "resilience layers" and helps the lab identify unforeseen misuses, such as "medical spam."

## Notable Quotes
> "If you really can predict the next word out of Einstein's mouth, you are at least as smart as Einstein." — **Greg Brockman**

> "In the words of Ilya [Sutskever], he always says that you have to suffer. If you're not suffering, you're not building value." — **Greg Brockman**

> "One observation I have is that the right choices are extremely specific to the facts of the technology... It's not just about the model itself; it's really about how they integrate into the world with a society that is resilient." — **Greg Brockman**

> "I think I've just learned to just keep going for something that's worth it. If you have a mission that matters, then the fact of you keep going through the ups and the downs... you just can't let those moments pull you off course." — **Greg Brockman**

briefings.title: Sen. Elizabeth Warren on Fed chair nominee Kevin Warsh, financial regulation and Iran
briefings.tldr: Senator Elizabeth Warren characterized Fed chair nominee Kevin Warsh as a "sock puppet" for Donald Trump, arguing his refusal to demonstrate independence disqualifies him, while simultaneously defending her regulatory record against accusations that she "killed" community banking.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Senator Elizabeth Warren characterized Fed chair nominee Kevin Warsh as a "sock puppet" for Donald Trump, arguing his refusal to demonstrate independence disqualifies him, while simultaneously defending her regulatory record against accusations that she "killed" community banking.

## Federal Reserve Independence and Kevin Warsh
* **The "Sock Puppet" Critique:** Senator Warren argues that nominee Kevin Warsh failed to demonstrate the independence required for the Federal Reserve Chair. 
    * **Refusal to Disagree:** Warren noted that during her meetings and public hearings, Warsh would not cite a single economic or factual point of disagreement with Donald Trump, including the results of the 2020 election.
    * **Monetary vs. Regulatory Independence:** Warren criticized Warsh’s reported stance that he only needs to be independent regarding monetary policy, while leaving "the door open" for the President to influence other Fed activities like bank mergers or crypto regulation.
* **Presidential Influence:** Warren expressed concern that Trump is attempting to "terrify" Fed officials through threats of firing and criminal investigations to gain control over the economy ahead of the November elections.
    * **The "Tough Guy" Defense:** While Warsh claimed in private meetings to be a "tough guy" who could stand up to Trump, Warren contends his public performance proved otherwise.

## Financial Regulation and Private Credit
* **Response to Scott Bessent:** Warren rebutted Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s claim that her "overregulation" killed community banks and forced lending into the unregulated private credit market.
    * **Underregulation Argument:** She noted that the recent failures of the second, third, and fourth largest banks in U.S. history occurred because they were *underregulated*, not overregulated.
    * **Community Bank Consolidation:** Warren attributed the decline of community banks to "too-big-to-fail" giants buying them up, rather than regulatory pressure.
* **Private Credit Risks:** Warren warned that the growth of private credit creates a "regulatory arbitrage" similar to the conditions before the 2008 financial crisis.
    * **Legislative Goals:** She is advocating for better regulation of the private credit market to gain visibility into systemic risks, though she expressed skepticism about gaining Republican support for such measures.

## Housing and Domestic Priorities
* **Housing Supply Bill:** Warren identified the housing crisis as her top priority, citing a bill passed by the Senate with a large majority that aims to increase housing supply and remove private equity from the market.
    * **Legislative Stagnation:** She criticized the Republican-controlled House of Representatives for stalling the bill and called on Trump to use his influence to move the legislation forward.
* **Economic Stance:** Warren emphasized her focus on "transforming" an economy she views as "hip-deep in corruption," aiming to deliver lower costs for hardworking people rather than billionaires.

## Foreign Policy and Political Endorsements
* **Iran and Global Credibility:** Warren criticized Donald Trump’s handling of Iran, stating he "trashed America’s credibility" by tearing up the nuclear agreement without a viable alternative.
    * **Safety Concerns:** She argued that current military actions and the blockade are driving up domestic prices and making Americans less safe.
* **Endorsement of Graham Platner:** Warren defended her endorsement of Maine candidate Graham Platner despite his controversial past and comments.
    * **Economic Alignment:** She justified her support by focusing on Platner's stance on the 2008 financial crisis, specifically his frustration that "not one banker went to jail."

> "What Donald Trump wants is a Fed that is under his control. He wants a sock puppet, and he's been very clear about that... Kevin Warsh's job yesterday was just to show just a little tiny bit of independence and he just couldn't do that." — **Sen. Elizabeth Warren**

> "It's a little hard to call the banks overregulated when just three years ago the second, third, and fourth biggest bank failures in America occurred because they were underregulated." — **Sen. Elizabeth Warren**

> "Donald Trump is trashing America's credibility and America's reputation as a moral force all around the world... He tore up [the Iran agreement] and you know what Mr. Dealmaker got in return? Nothing. Zero." — **Sen. Elizabeth Warren**

briefings.title: Tesla Q1 2026 Financial Results and Q&A Webcast
briefings.tldr: Tesla is pivoting into a massive $25B+ capital investment phase for 2026, prioritizing the "revolutionary" scale-up of Optimus, AI-5 chip architecture, and unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) over short-term free cash flow.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Tesla is pivoting into a massive $25B+ capital investment phase for 2026, prioritizing the "revolutionary" scale-up of Optimus, AI-5 chip architecture, and unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) over short-term free cash flow.

## AI, Autonomy, and Chip Infrastructure
*   **FSD Software Roadmap:** Version 14.3 was a major architectural update, while the upcoming Version 15 (targeted for late 2026/early 2027) will be a complete software overhaul running on AI 4 hardware.
    *   The goal for V15 is to move beyond human-level safety to "unsupervised" autonomy globally where legal.
*   **Robotaxi Expansion:** Operations have expanded to Dallas and Houston using the same software source as the Bay Area. Management emphasized a shift in strategy where the vehicle is viewed primarily as the "delivery mechanism" for FSD.
*   **Vertical Integration (Terrafab):** Tesla is constructing a "Research Chip Fab" on the Giga Texas campus. 
    *   **Strategic Rationale:** Elon Musk stated the fab is not for leverage over suppliers but because the industry cannot grow logic and memory fast enough to meet Tesla’s future AI demands.
*   **Custom Silicon:** The AI 5 chip has "taped out" and is expected to be the best edge inference chip for compute; development has already begun on AI 6 and Dojo 3.

## The Evolution of Optimus
*   **Production Timeline:** Initial production for Optimus is slated to begin in Fremont around late July or August 2026. A second Optimus factory is under construction at Giga Texas, with production starting in Summer 2027.
*   **V3 Design Reveal:** Expected by mid-2026. Musk noted a hesitation to reveal the "polished" V3 design early because competitors perform "frame-by-frame analysis" to copy Tesla’s technology.
*   **Technical Intelligence:** Optimus will use xAI’s Grok for "orchestration" (high-level management) and voice interaction.
    *   The robot is designed with enough local intelligence to operate for "several hours" without a cellular or Wi-Fi connection, similar to how Tesla vehicles drive safely offline.

## 2026 Financial Outlook and Capital Expenditures
*   **CapEx Surge:** CFO Vibhav Taneja projected 2026 CapEx to exceed $25 billion. This supports the ramp-up of six factories, AI infrastructure, and the Texas chip fab.
*   **Free Cash Flow:** Management expects negative free cash flow for the remainder of 2026 due to this heavy investment cycle.
*   **Margins and Revenue:**
    *   **Auto Margins:** Improved sequentially to 19.2% (excluding credits), aided by one-time warranty true-downs of $230M.
    *   **Order Backlog:** Q1 ended with the highest order backlog in over two years, with significant demand growth in France and Germany (150%+ QoQ).
    *   **Energy Margins:** Reached a record 39.5% gross margin, though this was boosted by $250M in one-time tariff recognitions.

## Manufacturing and Energy Storage
*   **Production Constraints:** The primary limiter for vehicle growth is currently "battery pack capacity" rather than cell supply. Tesla is retooling its Reno facility and ramping 4680 cell production in Berlin to address this.
*   **New Product Ramps:** Cybercab and Semi-truck are in the "slow S-curve" of initial production. Musk expects "exponential" growth for these lines toward the end of 2026.
*   **Megapack 3:** Production is scheduled to begin later this year at a new factory outside Houston to meet "very strong" global demand for energy storage.
*   **Solar Strategy:** To combat a stall in residential solar, Tesla introduced a new lease product to capture tax credits and launched a "best-in-class" mounting system and proprietary panel.

> "I think Optimus will be our biggest product, not just Tesla's biggest product ever, but probably the biggest product ever." — **Elon Musk, CEO**

> "We have evolved our vehicle sales strategy where we now emphasize FSD as a product and vehicle as only the delivery mechanism." — **Vibhav Taneja, CFO**

> "We just anticipate hitting the wall if we don't make chips ourselves... the rate at which the industry is growing in logic but even more so in memory is just [insufficient]." — **Elon Musk, CEO**

> "While this may seem a lot [referring to $25B CapEx] and we will have the impact of negative free cash flow for the rest of the year, we believe this is the right strategy to position the company for the next era." — **Vibhav Taneja, CFO**

briefings.title: Treasury Sec. Scott Bessent testifies before Senate panel on Trump's budget request — 4/22/26
briefings.tldr: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent presented an $11.5 billion FY 2027 budget request, a 12% reduction from the prior year, focusing on technology-driven efficiency, the implementation of the "Working Families Tax Cuts Act," and establishing U.S. leadership in digital assets through the GENIUS Act.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent presented an $11.5 billion FY 2027 budget request, a 12% reduction from the prior year, focusing on technology-driven efficiency, the implementation of the "Working Families Tax Cuts Act," and establishing U.S. leadership in digital assets through the GENIUS Act. While the administration emphasized improved IRS performance and middle-class relief, minority members challenged the efficacy of cutting IRS enforcement and the impact of sanctions policy on rising domestic energy costs.

## FY 2027 Budget Priorities and IRS Modernization
* **Spending Reductions:** The Department of Treasury is requesting $11.5 billion, a $1.5 billion (12%) decrease from FY 2026.
    * **Efficiency vs. Funding:** Secretary Bessent argued that prior "bloat" is being replaced by technology, noting that enforcement recoveries rose 12% last year despite budget cuts.
* **IRS Workforce & Direct File:**
    * **Staffing Levels:** Ranking Member Jack Reed noted the IRS has lost 28,000 employees since the start of the Trump administration, with another 4,000-person reduction proposed.
    * **Program Cancellations:** The administration officially ended the "Direct File" program. Secretary Bessent defended this by citing high costs ($138 per filer) compared to the public-private "Free File" alternative.
* **Operational Modernization:**
    * **Digital-First Strategy:** 98% of taxpayers now file electronically, with 90% receiving refunds within 21 days.
    * **Vendor Accountability:** Chairman Bill Hagerty praised the cancellation of contracts with Booz Allen Hamilton following a massive data breach, citing a failure to properly vet personnel who leaked sensitive taxpayer information.

## Tax Policy and "Working Families" Initiatives
* **Signature Policy Implementation:** The Treasury is prioritizing the "Working Families Tax Cuts Act," which provides relief on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
    * **No Tax on Tips:** Over 7 million filers claimed an average deduction of $7,000.
    * **No Tax on Overtime:** 28 million filers claimed an average deduction of $3,100.
    * **Seniors’ Relief:** 34 million seniors claimed an enhanced deduction averaging $7,500.
* **Trump Accounts:** The budget supports a pilot program for "Trump Accounts," which has seen 5.5 million accounts opened and 1.3 million children eligible for a $1,000 contribution to foster long-term financial security.
* **Paid Family Leave:** Senator Deb Fischer highlighted the expansion and permanence of the Paid Family and Medical Leave tax credit; Bessent committed to issuing finalized guidance for employers by early summer 2026.

## Digital Assets and Global Economic Leadership
* **The GENIUS Act:** The Treasury is requesting $4.8 million across departmental offices and FinCEN to implement the regulatory framework for stablecoins.
    * **US Leadership:** Chairman Hagerty emphasized that regulatory certainty is required to ensure the U.S. remains the home of financial innovation and protects the U.S. dollar's status as the world reserve currency.
* **Trade and Reciprocity:** Secretary Bessent highlighted efforts to reset global trade by negotiating reciprocal agreements to reduce dependence on competitors like China, particularly in the shipping and pharmaceutical sectors.

## National Security, Sanctions, and Energy
* **Sanctions Policy:** Senator Chris Coons questioned the administration on "sanctions relief" for Russia and Iran during the ongoing conflict, alleging it provided Russia with $150 million in daily revenue.
    * **Global Supply Strategy:** Secretary Bessent countered that temporary relief was necessary to prevent global oil prices from reaching $150/barrel, which would have severely impacted the American consumer and vulnerable allies.
* **Financial Intelligence:** The budget seeks increased funding for the Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence to trace and sanction illicit financial networks.
* **Foreign Influence Concerns:** Senator Chris Van Hollen raised questions regarding potential "swap lines" for the UAE and alleged linkages to private Trump family crypto ventures; Secretary Bessent denied any knowledge of the private investments or specific linkages to Treasury policy.

## Community Development and Rural Outreach
* **CDFI Cuts:** The budget proposes a 60% cut to the Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFI) fund. 
    * **Rural Focus:** Bessent argued that the program had become "partisan" but highlighted a new $100 million allocation specifically for rural areas to support daycares and small businesses in states like Nebraska and Maine.
* **Rural Service Access:** Senator Susan Collins expressed concern over the closure of Taxpayer Assistance Centers in Maine, noting that some residents now face a 10-hour round trip for in-person help. Bessent committed to reviewing these closures to ensure rural accessibility.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "America is unstoppable because its economy is unstoppable. ... I take that commitment very seriously, not only ensuring that every dollar in our budget is thoughtfully executed, but also that every dollar collected, deposited, or dispersed through Treasury is secure and timely."
— **Scott Bessent**, Secretary of the Treasury

> "No successful company would underinvest in its revenue collection mechanism. The IRS itself acknowledges that every dollar the agency invests in enforcement brings $11 back from tax cheats. Cutting IRS funding is a proven windfall for the rich."
— **Senator Jack Reed** (Ranking Member)

> "There is no better example of delivering meaningful change for everyday Americans than President Trump's working families tax cuts... We are delivering tax relief to working families."
— **Scott Bessent**, Secretary of the Treasury

> "America must be the global leader in this sector [digital assets] if we want to retain our position as the world's reserve currency."
— **Senator Bill Hagerty** (Chairman)

**TL;DR**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent presented a $11.5 billion FY2027 budget request, representing a 12% reduction aimed at streamlining the IRS through technology and implementing the "Working Families Tax Cuts Act," while facing scrutiny from Democrats over reduced tax enforcement and sanctions efficacy.

## FY2027 Budget Strategy and IRS Modernization
* **Budget Reduction:** Secretary Bessent proposed an $11.5 billion budget, a $1.5 billion (12%) decrease from the previous year. He characterized this as a shift toward efficiency and "outcomes over outlays."
* **IRS Headcount and Efficiency:** 
    * The IRS has reduced its workforce by approximately 28,000 employees since the start of the administration, with a further 4,000-person reduction planned. 
    * Bessent argued that technology—including AI and digital-first filing—has allowed for a 12% increase in enforcement recoveries ($41 billion total) despite lower staffing levels.
* **Service Metrics:** Treasury is introducing new performance metrics, such as "Assistor Service Rate" and "Enterprise Service Completion Rate," to better track how digital and automated systems serve taxpayers compared to traditional phone support.
* **Closing Assistance Centers:** Senator Susan Collins (R-ME) expressed concern over the closure of Taxpayer Assistance Centers in rural Maine, noting that some residents now face a 10-hour round trip for in-person help. Bessent committed to reviewing the "10-hour problem."

## Tax Policy and the Working Families Tax Cuts Act
* **Implementation Progress:** The Treasury is currently implementing guidance for the "Working Families Tax Cuts Act," which includes signature policies such as "No Tax on Tips" and "No Tax on Overtime."
* **Refund Data:** Bessent reported that average tax refunds for the current filing season are up 11–13% over the prior year.
    * **No Tax on Tips:** Over 7 million filers claimed an average deduction of $7,000.
    * **No Tax on Overtime:** 28 million filers claimed an average deduction of over $3,100.
    * **Seniors:** 34 million seniors claimed an enhanced deduction averaging $7,500.
* **Trump Accounts:** Nearly 5.5 million "Trump Accounts" have been opened to foster long-term financial security, with 1.3 million children eligible for a $1,000 pilot program contribution.
* **Direct File Shutdown:** Bessent defended the decision to terminate the "Direct File" program, arguing it cost $138 per person to administer ($72 million total for 300,000 users) and that the public-private "Free File" partnership is more cost-effective.

## Digital Assets and the "Genius Act"
* **Regulatory Framework:** Treasury is prioritizing the implementation of the "Genius Act," which establishes the first U.S. regulatory framework for stablecoins.
* **Strategic Funding:** The budget requests $1.8 million for departmental offices and $3 million for FinCEN to drive innovation and expertise in digital assets.
* **Global Leadership:** Bessent emphasized that providing regulatory clarity for digital assets is essential to maintaining the U.S. dollar’s status as the world’s reserve currency and ensuring the U.S. leads in payment technology.

## National Security and Geopolitical Finance
* **Sanctions Discrepancy:** Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) challenged the Secretary on reports that Iran and Russia have gained significant revenue via sanctions relief. Bessent disputed the $14 billion figure cited by Coons as a "myth," arguing that limited relief was necessary to prevent global oil prices from spiking to $150/barrel.
* **UAE Swap Line:** Bessent confirmed that the UAE and other Gulf allies have requested "swap lines" through the Exchange Stabilization Fund to maintain order in dollar funding markets, though he denied any linkage to the President's private business ventures.
* **Illicit Activity in Maine:** Senator Collins highlighted over 200 illegal marijuana grow houses in Maine linked to Chinese transnational criminal organizations. Bessent pledged that IRS Criminal Investigations and FinCEN would prioritize dismantling the associated money laundering operations.

## Contractor Accountability
* **Booz Allen Hamilton:** Chairman Hagerty and Secretary Bessent discussed the cancellation of contracts with Booz Allen Hamilton following a massive data breach of taxpayer information.
* **Vetting Failure:** Bessent described the breach as "premeditated" and "egregious," stating the firm failed to properly screen employees who weaponized sensitive data. He signaled a broader Treasury-wide loss of confidence in the contractor’s ability to safeguard information.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We haven't seen that in educational outcomes, we haven't seen that in healthcare outcomes—that more money equals better outcomes. And at the IRS thus far, we believe in outcomes." — **Secretary Scott Bessent** on cutting the IRS budget.

> "No successful company would underinvest in its revenue collection mechanism. The IRS itself acknowledges that every dollar the agency invests in enforcement brings $11 back from tax cheats." — **Senator Jack Reed**

> "This was an egregious attack on the privacy of thousands of American taxpayers... we no longer have confidence in that firm's ability to screen, vet, and deploy contractors within the IRS or indeed the entire Treasury Department." — **Secretary Scott Bessent** regarding Booz Allen Hamilton.

> "The U.S. has to lead here. We are the technological leader in the world; we should be the payments leader in the world." — **Secretary Scott Bessent** on digital asset regulation.

briefings.title: Trump’s Former Advisors Predict How His War with Iran Ends (w/ H.R. McMaster & Matt Pottinger)
briefings.tldr: Former National Security advisors H.R. McMaster and Matt Pottinger argue that the Iranian regime is fundamentally unstable and nearing collapse, advocating for a "counter-blockade" strategy while warning that a severely downsized National Security Council (NSC) risks losing the "peripheral vision" necessary for long-term competition with China.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Former National Security advisors H.R. McMaster and Matt Pottinger argue that the Iranian regime is fundamentally unstable and nearing collapse, advocating for a "counter-blockade" strategy while warning that a severely downsized National Security Council (NSC) risks losing the "peripheral vision" necessary for long-term competition with China.

## NSC Structure and Presidential Decision-Making
* **Staffing Reductions:** The current NSC policy staff has been reduced to approximately 36 people, down from a peak of nearly 200 during the Biden administration and 108 at the end of the first Trump term.
    * **Strategic Risk:** Matt Pottinger notes that while a small staff prevents territorial disputes, it makes "technically difficult strategy"—such as AI and semiconductor competition—nearly impossible to manage from the Oval Office due to sheer complexity.
* **The "Deep State" Narrative:** H.R. McMaster suggests that because President Trump was convinced his own staff was the "Deep State," he took a "cleaver" to the NSC, leading to inconsistencies in policy communication and integration.
* **Guarding Presidential Judgment:** McMaster emphasizes the National Security Advisor’s role as the "guardian of the president’s independence," which requires presenting multiple, distinct options rather than a single "shiny option" preferred by the bureaucracy.
    * **Problem Framing:** McMaster utilizes a "design thinking" approach: framing the challenge, identifying assumptions, and listing obstacles before ever discussing specific actions.

## Iran: Conflict, Nuclear Ambitions, and Regime Change
* **Regime Stability:** McMaster predicts a **75% chance** that the Iranian regime will not survive the next two years, citing the murder of 40,000 of its own citizens and a lack of organized internal opposition.
* **Counter-Blockade Strategy:** Pottinger defends the use of a counter-blockade against Iranian oil exports.
    * **Economic Pinch:** The goal is to ensure Iran does not benefit from oil exports while they attempt to close the Strait of Hormuz, forcing the regime to feel the same economic pain as its neighbors.
* **The Nuclear Divide:** A fundamental disagreement exists between the former Trump advisors and the Sullivan/Finer team regarding Iranian intent.
    * **The Trump View:** McMaster and Pottinger believe Iran has been actively pursuing a nuclear arsenal for decades.
    * **The Biden/Intel View:** Sullivan and Finer argue Iran uses the program as "leverage" and "option-buying" but has not had an active weapons program since 2003.
* **Ground Operations:** Pottinger counsels extreme caution regarding U.S. ground troops, noting the "character of warfare" has changed post-2022, with 90% of casualties in modern conflict (like Ukraine) coming from drones. McMaster suggests "limited missions" to take key terrain/islands might be necessary, but full regime change would likely come from the Iranian people or internal military splinters.

## China and the "Detente" Trap
* **Calibrated Confrontation vs. Detente:** Pottinger describes current U.S. policy as a "detente," which he views as a strategic mistake. He argues for a return to "calibrated confrontation" to prevent Beijing from using the time to catch up in AI and military strength.
* **Technological Offset:** Pottinger expresses concern over rethinking export controls on AI chips. He believes AI must remain a "third offset" that provides the U.S. an absolute—not just relative—technological advantage.
* **Regional Interconnectivity:** McMaster argues that China is a "huge loser" if the Iranian regime falls. China’s influence in the Middle East is currently predicated on its perceived ability to "constrain" Iran; if the regime changes, Gulf states will likely lose patience with Beijing’s previous support for Tehran.

## Notable Quotes

> "In the long term, the regime's done. They're finished. They murdered 40,000 of their own people. The Iranian people are ready for the change... these regimes only have to be stronger than any organized opposition to survive, so this could be a lengthy transition. But they're finished." — **H.R. McMaster**

> "The NSC is the president's eyes and ears and also his peripheral vision on what the consequences of various policies will be... When you've got 36 people, that basically means that things are not being surfaced to the president; everything is led from the president down." — **Matt Pottinger**

> "One of the functions of the National Security Advisor... is to be the guardian of the president's independence of judgment. And a way to do that is to insist on multiple options." — **H.R. McMaster**

> "You’re not going to take from us in negotiation things you couldn’t take from us in battle. And that’s why I think the war’s going to continue." — **Matt Pottinger** (characterizing the Iranian perspective)

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: Lutnick testifies on Trump’s Commerce Department budget request before Senate committee
briefings.tldr: Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick defended the Trump administration’s FY2027 budget, touting a "Golden Age" of domestic manufacturing and semiconductor investment while facing sharp bipartisan criticism over proposed deep cuts to economic development agencies and the management of $21 billion in remaining broadband funds.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick defended the Trump administration’s FY2027 budget, touting a "Golden Age" of domestic manufacturing and semiconductor investment while facing sharp bipartisan criticism over proposed deep cuts to economic development agencies and the management of $21 billion in remaining broadband funds.

## Economic Strategy and Trade Policy
* **Reshoring and Manufacturing:** Secretary Lutnick highlighted record-setting domestic investments, including a $200 billion commitment from Micron for semiconductors and a $550 billion trade deal with Japan involving nuclear and natural gas projects.
    * **Industry Targets:** Focus remains on steel, aluminum, copper, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors through Section 232 actions.
* **Trade Performance:** Lutnick claimed the administration has dramatically reduced the trade deficit, reaching a 16-year low in October 2025, with exports increasing to $3.4 trillion.
* **International Relations:** Senator Shaheen challenged Lutnick’s rhetoric regarding Canada (notably a comment that their economy "sucks"), arguing it has led to a 30% drop in Canadian tourism to states like New Hampshire. 
    * **Lutnick’s Response:** He defended the stance, citing Canada’s "disrespectful" treatment of U.S. spirits and dairy under USMCA.
* **Tariff Impact:** Senator Gillibrand raised concerns that tariffs act as a "ton of bricks" on small businesses relying on imported inputs. 
    * **Domestic Focus:** Lutnick countered that "if you build in America, you don’t have to pay the tariff," framing them as a necessary tool to reverse the "hollowing out" of U.S. industry.

## Broadband (BEAD) and Infrastructure
* **Funding Disputes:** A central point of tension was the remaining $21 billion in "non-deployment" funds within the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) program.
    * **Discretionary Concerns:** Chairman Moran expressed concern that a "catch-all" provision in the statute might allow the Department to divert these funds away from actual broadband connectivity.
    * **Precision Agriculture:** Senator Fischer urged the Department to ensure these funds support "precision agriculture" to maximize economic development in rural areas.
* **Status Update:** Lutnick reported that 54 states and territories are currently drawing down the initial $21 billion for deployment, with a plan for the remaining funds expected within two months.

## National Security and Technology Oversight
* **Export Controls:** Senators Coons and Shaheen questioned the licensing of H200 AI chips to China, suggesting they provide the PLA with advanced war-fighting capabilities.
    * **Lutnick’s Defense:** He asserted that the U.S. is not selling its "best" chips (specifically the Blackwell architecture) and that President Trump is balancing a complex relationship with President Xi.
* **Rare Earth Minerals:** Senator Van Hollen questioned a $1.6 billion federal stake in "USA Rare Earth," alleging a lack of transparency and a potential conflict of interest involving Lutnick’s former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald. Lutnick maintained the deal was vital to breaking China’s "chokehold" on critical minerals.
* **Quantum Computing:** The budget proposes a 32% cut to quantum research at NIST. Lutnick argued this shift is intentional, as the "private sector is leading the charge," and the government should transition to a coordinating role.

## Proposed Agency Cuts and Reorganization
* **Program Eliminations:** The budget proposes the total elimination of the Economic Development Administration (EDA) and the Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA).
* **NIST and NOAA:** Lutnick defended a 54% cut to NIST and a 27% cut to NOAA, suggesting the agencies have "drifted" from their core missions.
* **Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP):** Despite bipartisan support for MEP, Lutnick defended proposed cuts by citing Inspector General reports that alleged "excessive compensation" for executives and inaccurate performance statistics.
* **Census 2030:** Lutnick proposed using the U.S. Postal Service to conduct the census to save costs on hiring and training 500,000 temporary workers. 
    * **Criticism:** Senator Schatz cited GAO studies suggesting letter carriers are not trained for this role and that the move could delay mail delivery.

## Notable Quotes

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The "relentless exponential" growth of AI and crypto is converging toward "agentic commerce," where autonomous agents move from simple task automation to becoming fully independent economic actors capable of transacting, hiring, and self-funding via blockchains.

## The Intersection of AI Productivity and AGI
* **Redefining AGI:** Ali Yahya defines Artificial General Intelligence not as a shifting technical goalpost, but as the moment an agent becomes **"fully independently economically valuable."**
    * This means an agent acting as an end-to-end employee or founder that can create value and remain self-sustaining without human intervention.
* **The Productivity Leap:** AI has fundamentally collapsed the cost of entry for startups. 
    * **Personal Output:** Yahya notes that using AI tools part-time allows him to be more productive in software engineering than he was as a full-time engineer at Google Brain.
    * **Team Efficiency:** A single founder can now accomplish what previously required a team of 5–10 people, though Yahya argues that large organizations (1,000+ people) leveraging AI will still maintain a massive competitive advantage (10x–100x) over smaller teams.
* **The "Alpha" Problem in Trading:** Yahya is skeptical of consumer-facing AI trading agents.
    * **Market Efficiency:** If everyone uses the same base model (like ChatGPT) to trade, "alpha" (market-beating edge) disappears by definition.
    * **Professional Edge:** Real value lies in professionals fine-tuning agents on proprietary data to create differentiated strategies.

## The Five Stages of Agentic Autonomy
Building on Stripe co-founder John Collison’s framework, Yahya outlines the progression toward a fully agentic economy:
1. **Stage 1: Tedium Removal:** Automating the entry of payment information and form-filling.
2. **Stage 2: Descriptive Search:** Agents find specific items at the best price based on user articulation.
3. **Stage 3: Delegation:** Users provide a high-level goal and a budget; the agent executes the end-to-end purchase.
4. **Stage 4: Anticipation:** The agent knows the user so well it purchases necessary items before the user even asks.
5. **Stage 5: Agent-to-Agent Commerce:** Agents transact with other agents for resources like compute, data, or skills using smart contracts and stablecoins—a system where the agent might even raise its own capital.

## The Case for Crypto Fundamentals and Privacy
* **Sentiment vs. Reality:** While crypto sentiment is low, fundamentals are at all-time highs.
    * **Stablecoin Growth:** Currently $200B–$300B in circulating supply with over **$1 trillion in monthly transaction volume.**
    * **Regulatory Clarity:** The "Genius Bill" and the entry of major TradFi institutions have de-risked the space more than ever before.
* **Privacy as a Business Moat:** Historically, blockchains prioritized verifiability over privacy, but mainstream adoption requires encrypted, programmable networks.
    * **Defensibility:** Public data is easy to "port" or copy. Encrypted data creates higher switching costs and stronger network effects because moving private data incurs the risk of "unveiling" sensitive information.
    * **Pragmatic Compliance:** Yahya rejects "uncompromising" end-to-end privacy as a niche dead-end. Success requires **programmable privacy** that allows for legal compliance (e.g., sanctions) while protecting user data.

## Vertical Integration in Venture Capital
* **The a16z "Platform" Model:** Unlike traditional firms, a16z crypto operates with a 70-person team where only ~10 are investors.
    * **The Support Staff:** 60+ people focus on "projecting power" for founders, including a research team of experts in distributed systems and a regulatory team featuring former SEC directors (Bill Hinman) and top-tier legal partners (Miles Jennings).
* **The "Uber" Paradigm:** Modern startups are no longer just building tools for existing industries; they are building vertically integrated replacements (like Uber replacing taxis). This requires investors to provide specialized help in policy, talent, and go-to-market strategies that technical founders often lack.

## Notable Quotes

> "It is funny that we're now at a point where the sentiment about crypto is close to an all-time low at the same time that the fundamentals are very clearly at an all-time high." — **Ali Yahya**

> "The unicorn is obviously a senior engineer who is extremely adaptable and willing to reinvent themselves overnight by throwing out the previous playbook and completely adapting to the new [AI] tools." — **Ali Yahya**

> "We have digital intelligence; the next big unlock will be physical intelligence [robotics]." — **Ali Yahya**
